summary: The paper compares QAOA, QAOAz, and a Quantum Walk Optimisation Algorithm (QWOA) for discrete Markowitz portfolio optimization with n=8 assets (16 qubits). In noiseless simulations up to p=19 layers, QWOA reduces the search space from 2^16=65,536 states (QAOA) to 266 valid portfolios and amplifies the optimal portfolio to >40% probability in one dataset, while QAOAz fails to amplify the optimum (<10^-9 probability). All results are obtained on classical simulation with no comparison to classical portfolio optimizers.

experiments.description: Numerical simulation of portfolio optimisation using the original QAOA with soft constraint penalty encoding on two real-market datasets (Data Set A and B), compared against QAOAz and QWOA.

algorithm.variant: QAOA with soft constraint penalty encoding
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Randomly generated initial ⃗γ and ⃗t values uniformly distributed between 0 and 2π

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Two qubits per asset encode three discrete positions: |01⟩ long, |10⟩ short, |00⟩ no position; |11⟩ is degenerate with no position
problem_formulation.objective_function: c(z) = λ Σ_{i,j=1}^n σ_{ij} z_i z_j - (1-λ) Σ_{i=1}^n r_i z_i, with penalty ζ(z)=ϵ(A-Σ_i z_i)^2 for QAOA
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Soft constraint via quadratic penalty term added to the objective

problem_instance.description: Discrete mean-variance Markowitz portfolio optimisation with 8 assets and net position constraint A=4
problem_instance.dataset_name: Data Set A and Data Set B
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Daily adjusted close prices from Yahoo Finance; adjusted close used to account for corporate actions such as dividends
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 15 repeats per algorithm using the same set of randomly generated initial parameters; BFGS used for classical parameter optimisation; results reported as mean and standard deviation across repeats

implementation_details.classical_solver: BFGS; brute-force classical iteration used to obtain the global optimum for comparison
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Historical price data selected from Yahoo Finance; objective and covariance estimated from data
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Expectation values of return and risk computed from output state probabilities

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: Improves with p but generally worse than QAOAz and QWOA

speedup_claims.factor: QWOA mixing circuit complexity O(n^2) per iteration
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper argues the polynomial overhead is outweighed by the smaller search space and better convergence, but no formal speedup proof is given.

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Randomly generated initial ⃗γ and ⃗t values uniformly distributed between 0 and 2π

problem_formulation.objective_function: c(z) = λ Σ_{i,j=1}^n σ_{ij} z_i z_j - (1-λ) Σ_{i=1}^n r_i z_i
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Strict feasibility via indexing to the valid non-degenerate subspace; no penalty term
problem_formulation.num_ancilla_qubits: O(log n) ancilla for indexing; O(log M(n,A)) index register and O(n) output register
